content: {"summary":"Memory creep in fraud‑scorer and redis‑features latency spikes have occurred before; the typical stopgap is to set vm.overcommit_memory=1 and restart the scorer before hitting OOM limits.","likely_cause":"Redis hit its maxmemory limit (noeviction) causing OOM path errors, which forces fraud‑scorer pods to accumulate memory and eventually be OOMKilled.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Prior similar incidents have been observed when redis‑features latency spikes occur","evidence_ids":["RB-006#2"],"quote":"seen on fraud-scorer-01.prod.internal and fraud-scorer-02.prod.internal, mostly when redis-features latency spikes"},{"text":"During those spikes fraud‑scorer pods have been OOMKilled","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#1"],"quote":"Second `OOMKilled` on fraud-scorer-02."},{"text":"A quick fix is to set vm.overcommit_memory=1 on the redis node","evidence_ids":["RB-019#3"],"quote":"ssh redis-features-01.prod.internal 'sudo sysctl -w vm.overcommit_memory=1' # then fix it at the source"},{"text":"Another stopgap is to restart the fraud‑scorer deployment before the memory limit is reached","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#2"],"quote":"restart before the limit, not after."},{"text":"The root cause is Redis reaching maxmemory, triggering OOM path errors","evidence_ids":["RB-019#2"],"quote":"used_memory at maxmemory, noeviction -> OOM path"}],"next_checks":["Check current vm.overcommit_memory setting on redis-features-01","Inspect Redis INFO memory usage and maxmemory status","Monitor FRD‑E140 write‑refusal errors in fraud‑scorer logs","Watch for OOMKilled events on fraud‑scorer pods","Verify latency spikes with redis-cli --latency"]}
